name: Pinji
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Pinji (Gabon, Bantu B30): Glottolog cites only Grollemund 2006 classification work; no grammar/phonology located online.

sources.citation: Grollemund, Rebecca. 2006. Les Okande du Gabon, locuteurs d'une langue en danger (langue bantu du groupe B30) - Langue et culture. Mémoire de Master 2, Université Lumière-Lyon 2. 227 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Phonology/tone chapter is for Okande (kand1300), not Pinji; Pinji appears only in untoned ALGAB comparative consonant-reflex tables (ch. IV, pp. 202-217). Nothing on Pinji tone or stress.

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 2003. The B30 language group. In Derek Nurse & Gérard Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 371-391. London: Routledge. [author's offprint, 27 pp., DDL Lyon]
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2.2 'Suprasegmental phonology' (offprint p.12) covers vowel harmony and tone; 2.2.2 says T/Vo/Vi have H, L, HL, LH noun melodies and 'No reliable tonal data are available for N-B30 so far' (N-B30 = Pinzi, Kande, Himba). Pinzi forms in the chapter are transcribed without tone marks. Pinzi sketch p.3: main publications Jacquot (1978, 1983), VdV (1991a); dialectal differences noted.

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1991. Etude dialectométrique et lexicostatistique du groupe B 30 (Gabon). Pholia 6: 191-217.
sources.note: Nothing; Pinji (ﬁe-pinzi, P) only as a lexicostatistic taxon (P-K-H subgroup at 81-85.9%).

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1989. Doubles réflexes dans quelques langues du groupe Okani (Gabon). Pholia 4: 229-243.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.230: 'le système tonal du PB semble toujours être en place, au moins dans la plupart des parlers du groupe'; treats only Okani Sud (Tsogo, Vove, Viya), data for Okani Nord incl. Pinji declared insufficient.

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1988. Caractéristiques principales du groupe B 30 (Gabon). Pholia 3: 271-290. Lyon: CRLS, Université Lumière-Lyon 2.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; sec. 4.1 gives segmental traits of the six B30 lects (Pinji = parler 4); lexical reconstructions labelled 'tonalité incertaine' (p.284).

sources.citation: Kwenzi Mikala, J. T. 1987. Contribution à l'inventaire des parlers bantu du Gabon. Pholia 2: 103-110 (and other Pholia 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9 articles searched for Pinji).
sources.note: Nothing; lists 'epipinzi ou epinzipinzi (= apinji)' (p.109) as a Ngounié lect. No Pinji description anywhere in Pholia 1-9.
